description: Imports Stripe payments data — customers, charges, invoices, subscriptions, payouts and related objects — from the Stripe REST API, including optionally from connected accounts.

spec.apiVersionPinning: `Stripe-Version` REQUEST HEADER, injected on every request by StripeHTTPMixin._request_stream. Its value is not a literal in the source: it is `advanced.api_version` when the user sets it, otherwise the account's own default, read at startup from the `stripe-version` RESPONSE header of GET /v1/account. A conditional `Stripe-Account: <acct_id>` header is also sent per request to scope it to the platform account or a connected account.

configFields.name: credentials.access_token
configFields.description: Stripe API key. A key beginning with `rk_` is treated as restricted and triggers per-stream accessibility probing at discovery.

configFields.name: start_date
configFields.description: UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Data created before this is not replicated. Defaults to 30 days before the present.

configFields.name: capture_connected_accounts
configFields.description: When true, every non-exempt binding fans out into one subtask per connected account id, each sending its own `Stripe-Account` header.

configFields.name: advanced.api_version
configFields.description: Stripe dated API version (e.g. "2024-06-20", optionally with a codename suffix). Blank means use the account default. Streams whose MINIMUM_API_VERSION exceeds the effective version are dropped.

configFields.name: advanced.incremental_window_size
configFields.description: ISO 8601 duration, default P1D, bounded to [PT1M, P30D]. Caps how far forward one incremental sweep of /v1/events may advance.

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO 8601 duration between updates for this binding. The connector seeds every binding with PT5M.

configFields.name: schedule
configFields.description: Cron expression for an automatic re-backfill of this binding. Seeded with "0 0 * * *" for Accounts, ExternalAccountCards, ExternalBankAccount, Persons and ValueLists; empty for every other stream.

pathPlaceholders.parent_id: id of an ApplicationFees record (from /v1/application_fees, or from an event payload during incremental)

pathPlaceholders.subscription_item_id: id from items.data[] of a Subscriptions record listed at /v1/subscriptions?status=all

pathPlaceholders.value_list: id of a ValueLists record; sent as a query param, not a path segment

authTierRationale: The only credential the connector accepts is a single Stripe API key, supplied as estuary_cdk's `AccessToken` model and handed to `TokenSource(oauth_spec=None, ...)`. Because `oauth_spec` is None the CDK never performs a token exchange; it emits `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every request. The user creates the key self-serve in the Stripe dashboard — no OAuth app registration and no refresh token. Restricted keys (`rk_`) are supported and merely narrow which streams get discovered.

unionMisfits.where: streams[].pull.incremental (all event-driven child and split-child streams)
unionMisfits.description: A single PullSpec cannot express the two-legged incremental read used by every child stream. Leg 1 lists /v1/events filtered to the child's event types; leg 2 then re-fetches the child collection of each parent named in an event, using exactly the backfill path/params/paginator. Only leg 1 is recorded in `pull.incremental`; leg 2 is identical to `pull.backfill` and is invoked once per distinct parent id seen in the event page.

`incrementalParam` assumes a server-side LOWER bound. Stripe's /v1/events reads send only an UPPER bound, `created[lte] = min(now-60s, cursor + advanced.incremental_window_size)`, and Stripe serves results newest-first; the resume lower bound (the log cursor) is applied CLIENT-SIDE by breaking out of the page loop when an event older than the cursor is seen. Recording created[lte] as `incrementalParam` would be actively wrong, so it is null and the value is described here instead.

The stream list is static (a literal STREAMS table plus a REGIONAL_STREAMS table), but discovery still makes network calls: with a restricted `rk_` key each stream's list endpoint is probed and 401/403/400-"not set up to use" responses drop the binding; the three regional Issuing streams are probed unconditionally; UsageRecords is probed via a deliberate invalid-id path; and streams whose MINIMUM_API_VERSION exceeds the effective Stripe-Version are dropped. This is a static list intersected with a live accessibility check rather than either `static` or `discovered`.

With `capture_connected_accounts` enabled the connector first enumerates every connected account id by sweeping GET /v1/accounts partitioned into `created[gte]`/`created[lte]` time chunks across 10 concurrent workers, then multiplies every non-exempt binding into one subtask per account id. This request multiplier is a connector-wide fan-out with no place in the schema.

abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No static header value is encoded anywhere. The two headers the connector adds are both runtime-resolved: `Stripe-Version` (config override, else the account default read back from the /v1/account response header) and `Stripe-Account` (the platform account id, or a connected account id when capture_connected_accounts is on). Both are described in apiVersionPinning instead of being asserted as constants.
abstained.streams[].pull.incremental.incrementalPa: No stream other than ValueListItems sends a server-side LOWER bound. Event-driven streams send only `created[lte]` (a ceiling) and rely on Stripe's newest-first ordering plus a client-side break once an event older than the log cursor is seen (api.py:191-193). The no-event list streams (Accounts, Files, FilesLink, BalanceTransactions, ValueLists) send NO date parameter at all — just limit + starting_after — and filter entirely client-side (api.py:840-893), so every incremental sweep re-reads pages from the newest record backwards until it crosses the cursor. Asserting an incrementalParam here would be silently wrong.
abstained.streams[].pull.snapshot: No binding is snapshot-only. Every binding registers both a fetch_page (backfill) and a fetch_changes (incremental) function, so the backfill/incremental split always applies.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: Recorded as `created` because that is the field every fetch function compares against the cursor, but the checkpointed cursor is not the record's own field in the event-driven case — it is the `created` of the /v1/events envelope record (+1ms), not of the emitted document. For ValueListItems and the no-event streams it genuinely is the document's `created`.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Recorded as `merge` because documents carry a meta op of c/u/d and Flow reduces on the key, but the connector never emits an explicit tombstone/delete document — deleted resources arrive as ordinary documents tagged op="d" (and Customers deletes are deliberately downgraded to "u"). Whether the destination materialises that as a delete is outside this source.
abstained.discovery: Left null because the stream list is a literal table in models.py, not read from the customer's schema. The live accessibility probing that gates that list is recorded in unionMisfits[2] rather than being dressed up as discovery.
abstained.streams[Authorizations|CardHolders|Trans: These three REGIONAL_STREAMS are in the shipped table and get bindings when the region/account allows, but they do not appear in the committed discover snapshot (the test account cannot reach them). Their paths and event types come from models.py; the pull shape is asserted from the shared base_object builder, not observed in a snapshot.
abstained.execution.continuity: Set to null deliberately, not skipped: this is a stateless polling HTTP connector. It creates no server-side object on Stripe — no webhook endpoint, no subscription, no cursor registered with Stripe. Pausing between ticks accrues nothing on the customer's side. The one thing WE can lose is the Events backfill page token: /v1/events has a ~30-day retention window and the code explicitly treats a 400 "aged out of our retention policy" on a checkpointed event id as end-of-stream (api.py:285-292), so a paused Events backfill past that window silently completes short rather than erroring. That risk is specific to the Events stream's backfill and did not fit `continuity`, which the schema scopes to log-mode connectors.
